messages:
alyssa: Heads up — noticed NaNs in outputs after switching to fp8 Flash variant on prod-like bench. Repro on dedicated infra (A100s). Logs attached.

mike: @alyssa can you paste the minimal repro? which kernel exactly? flash_attn_v2_fp8 or our fused path?

alyssa: repro snippet:
```python
x = torch.randn(2, 1024, 4096, dtype=torch.float32).to('cuda')
out = flash_attn(x, x, x, dtype='fp8_e4m3')  # using latest fp8 path
```
getting infs/NaNs near softmax, appears when sequence>512 and kv cache reused

sanjay: interesting. we saw saturation when scaling factors for fp8 were not updated for cached kvs. paged-attn reuses old scale leading to exponent blowup.

eva: perf-bot results: perf/regressions/1765432110 - latency +12% for chat benchmark when falling back to stable bf16, but throughput improved vs fp8 with NaN handling disabled :thinking:

perf-bot: [auto] benchmark: chat-1k-seq - before: 85ms p99, after(fp8): 98ms p99, errors: 0->3.2% NaN

mike: @sanjay can you dump the kv scale evolution from cache? maybe we need per-token dynamic max-scaling like in GPTQ papers

sanjay: dump:
```
kv_scale[0:10] = [0.0034, 0.0034, 0.0033, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0035]
```
0.0 entries correspond to pages that were zeroed via page-evict path bug (oops)

alyssa: found root cause: paged-attn page-evict zeroed buffer but we left old fp8 scale uninitialized (0) -> division by zero in dequant -> huge exponents -> softmax overflow

eva: quick fix PR: github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/4149 - initialize scale properly on evict and clamp exponent range in softmax

mike: good. add unit tests: sequence wrap-around, cached kv with mixed dtype, and stress on fp8 quant/clamp thresholds

sanjay: also adding log-sum-exp stable softmax fallback when max>threshold. that'll prevent saturation at cost of 1-2% perf.

alyssa: can we tune batching heuristics to avoid mixing freshly cached kv pages with new ones in same batch? mixing seems to amplify scale mismatches.

mike: yes — change: prefer homogeneous-kv batches for fp8 kernels. scheduler change + metric to track mixed-batch ratio.

perf-bot: [auto] perf/regressions/1765432160 - after PR: p99 90ms, errors 3.2% -> 0.1%, throughput -3%

eva: rolling patch to canary tomorrow. @oncall please watch NaN rate and newly introduced mixed-batch metrics :alarm_clock:

mike: plan: canary -> smoke tests -> roll to 10% -> full. revert ready if NaN>0.5% or latency p99 regresses >10%.

alyssa: thanks all. I'll add detailed repro and attach profiling traces (kernel timings + flops) in the PR.
